content:
Announcing mathlas: an open-source (Apache-2.0) MCP server that gives any agent (Claude Code, Cursor, anything MCP) a set of math tools designed around one discipline: every result is either an independently checkable fact or an honest "nothing". No tool calls an LLM; no API keys; runs locally.

  • search_existing_math: 3.68M-statement index (dense Qwen3 + BM25), self-recall benchmarks published in the repo
  • verify_formal: real Lean 4 kernel typecheck; search_formal_math: Loogle + LeanSearch proxy → mathlib declarations with provenance (Hit@5 0.96 on an index-verified gold set)
  • identify_constant (PSLQ, 50-digit re-verification), identify_sequence (exact OEIS term match), verify_numeric
  • applicability_checklist / mapping_scaffold: hypothesis decomposition so the agent judges applicability — the misapplication-catching layer I haven't seen elsewhere
  • a FunSearch-style sandboxed program-search harness and a web-augmentation loop (add_finding) that folds verified findings back into the live corpus

Repo + benchmarks: https://github.com/Archerkattri/mathlas · pip install mathlas-mcp
(uvx mathlas-mcp to run). Feedback, issues, and harsh review all welcome: particularly
from people who actually live in mathlib.
